rationale: Checked whether the runtime's drop-oldest egress policy can discard client work under the documented safety rationale. The rationale says dropping is safe because OmniPaxos resends lost messages, but outgoing_buf also carries ProposalForward (plain appends issued on a follower) and runtime TaggedProposal/Assigned messages, which neither core nor runtime resends. Recorded as a behavior with its applicability condition (the caller must keep draining outgoing_messages; the drop only occurs past the buffer cap), not as a defect claim, since sustained non-draining is a documented caller duty.

knowledge.statement: When the outgoing channel does not accept a message, messages accumulate in outgoing_buf; once its length exceeds the channel capacity (or max_outgoing_buffered), drain_outgoing_buf drops the oldest entries before retrying. The same buffer holds core protocol traffic pulled by flush_outgoing, including PaxosMsg::ProposalForward produced when a plain append is issued on a follower, and runtime control messages enqueued by try_dispatch_undispatched (TaggedProposal) and by Assigned replies. Core resends Promise/PrepareReq/Prepare/AcceptStopSign/StopSign-Decide but not ProposalForward, and the runtime does not resend TaggedProposal, so dropping those messages loses the corresponding client proposal (a tagged proposal then resolves only by timeout; a plain forwarded append is not retried at all). The configuration docs justify drop-oldest as safe because OmniPaxos tolerates lost messages, which covers protocol messages but not these client-origin ones.
knowledge.conditions: Runtime actor with outgoing channel backpressure sustained long enough for outgoing_buf to exceed its cap while client-origin messages are queued; the caller is expected to drain outgoing_messages continuously, so sustained non-draining is a caller-duty violation and bounds the applicability.
